terms.gloss: press hard, urge; (passive) be under pressure
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.5.1: urgēbar ab eō ad quem mīsī
Cic. Fam. 9.1.1: tot tantīsque rēbus urgēmur
terms.comment: Latin uses the verb: to be under pressure is urgērī; to put pressure on someone, urgēre or īnstāre.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: with the dative; ut and the subjunctive
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.13.3: īnstat et urget Catō
Cic. Att. 13.32.1: urgē, īnstā, perfice (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: urgēbar ab eō ad quem mīsī, et nōn habēbam exemplar
phrases.english: I was under pressure from the man I sent it to, and I had no copy

phrases.latin: etsī tot tantīsque rēbus urgēmur, ut nūllam adlevātiōnem quisquam nōn stultissimus spērāre dēbeat
phrases.english: although we are under such pressure from so many great troubles that only a fool would hope for any relief
Keep at it, press on, finish the job.
Press on and finish the job!

sources: Lewis & Short: urgeo · Lewis & Short: insto

Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
